messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0026. Final outcome: refund_full, amount $6.61 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: yes. Recommended action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and send the driver's account for review of the fake "I'm Here" arrival confirmation + flag_account.
Reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case: the driver cancelled and asserted a rider no-show, so it goes to NS-1/NS-2 [F3][RD-3 no] — more precisely [F3][NS-0]. Under NS-1 the fee stands only if all three elements hold. (i) is satisfied on its face: the trace shows a driver_tap at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. But (ii) fails decisively: at the tap the GPS put the car 600 m from the pickup, and the closest approach during the entire wait was 599 m — never within 200 m [F5][F1][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: the driver stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap [F5][NS-1], and the platform never recorded any arrival at the pickup point, with driver_arrived_at null [F4][NS-1]. The physical record contradicts the driver's own written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12]; system records override statements, and the rider's contemporaneous message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here" is consistent with the GPS [F9][F1][NS-1]. With (ii) and (iii) both unmet, NS-2 (or NS-3) applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full [F6][NS-2]. Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2 separately requires flag_account for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button [F5][F1][NS-2]; the trace also marks this ✓ and the profile field route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is satisfied for the driver (1 upheld no-show in 90 d), reinforcing RD-6 as grounds for account review — though RD-6 is not needed for the ruling itself [F17][RD-6]. The refund is issued as a voucher, and this remains a recommendation to Ryde [F6][NS-7]. Amount: the contested item is the fixed cancellation fee of $6.61 recorded in the fare fact, and no mileage/distance arithmetic is needed because the item is a flat fee [F3][F6][NS-2].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "Good news — we've refunded the $6.61 cancellation fee you were charged. We checked the driver's arrival record: the car was about 600 m from your pickup point the whole time, never closer than 599 m, and the app never logged an actual arrival. Your message saying you were waiting and saw no car matches that record. The $6.61 comes to you as a Ryde voucher. Thanks for flagging it — this case is also going to a human reviewer to look at the driver's account, since the \"I'm Here\" tap was made well outside the pickup area.", "driver": "Your account has been flagged for review after a no-show cancellation you reported. The trip record shows your \"I'm Here\" tap was made while your car was about 600 m from the pickup point, and you never came within 200 m or spent any time at the pickup during the wait — the app logged no arrival at all. Because of that, the $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. A human reviewer will look at your arrival confirmation and your recent no-show history before deciding what, if anything, happens to your account."}
